themes_detail.label: Street flooding and drainage crisis
themes_detail.summary: Standing water complaints spiked 1100% THIS WEEK (3 complaints vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks), coinciding with a 168% spike in water system complaints 3 weeks ago (113 vs. 42.1 avg), suggesting an emerging drainage or flooding emergency in CD 501.
evidence: Standing water complaints: 3 THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average (z-score: 6.35, 1100% increase)
Water system complaints: 113 complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 42.1 weekly average (168% spike, z-score: 4.03)
Pattern suggests underlying DEP or drainage infrastructure issue rather than temporary weather event
reporting_angles: Which neighborhoods in St. George/Stapleton are experiencing standing water; are there basement flooding or property damage reports?
Has DEP identified drainage infrastructure failures; what's the repair timeline and cost?

themes_detail.label: Tree overgrowth emergency in neighborhoods
themes_detail.summary: Overgrown tree and branch complaints surged 196% THIS WEEK (20 complaints vs. 6.8 weekly average), the highest-severity spike in the dataset (z-score: 8.08), indicating potential street obstruction, hazard, or visibility issues affecting resident safety and streetscape.
evidence: Overgrown tree/branches complaints: 20 THIS WEEK vs. 6.8 weekly average (196% spike, z-score: 8.08, highest spike in dataset)
Spike is geographically concentrated in CD 501 and emerged suddenly this week, not a gradual trend
Street light repair has been a repeated community board budget request, suggesting pre-existing visibility and maintenance concerns
reporting_angles: Which streets or blocks are most affected by overgrown trees; are they creating hazards for pedestrians, cyclists, or drivers?
Why did tree complaints spike this week—storm damage, seasonal growth, or backlog of deferred maintenance?

themes_detail.label: Missing and damaged street signs spike
themes_detail.summary: Street sign complaints (missing and damaged combined) surged 287% over the past 2 weeks: 5 missing signs 2 weeks ago vs. 1.1 weekly average, and 5 damaged signs 2 weeks ago vs. 1.5 average, creating navigation and safety hazards in the district.
evidence: Street sign - Missing: 5 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 1.1 weekly average (344% spike, z-score: 6.46)
Street sign - Damaged: 5 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 1.5 weekly average (233% spike, z-score: 4.04)
Combined signal suggests systematic infrastructure degradation or vehicle/weather damage affecting wayfinding across district
reporting_angles: Are missing and damaged signs concentrated in specific neighborhoods, and what's the cause (weather, accidents, vandalism, neglect)?
What's DOT's response time to street sign repair requests in this district versus citywide average?

themes_detail.label: Dumpster and litter management failures
themes_detail.summary: Over the past 2 weeks, dumpster complaints spiked 700% (5 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.6 average, z-score: 4.41) and litter basket requests surged 300% last week (8 vs. 2.0 average, z-score: 3.62), signaling sanitation service gaps or illegal dumping.
evidence: Dumpster complaints: 5 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.6 weekly average (700% spike, z-score: 4.41)
Litter basket requests: 8 complaints last week vs. 2.0 weekly average (300% spike, z-score: 3.62)
Unsanitary condition remains elevated in 90-day top 10 (505 complaints), suggesting broader cleanliness concerns
reporting_angles: Are residents complaining about overflowing or missing dumpsters, or are there illegal dumping sites emerging?
Has DSNY reduced collection frequency or basket maintenance in this district; what's the backlog?

themes_detail.label: Emergency response team activity spike
themes_detail.summary: Emergency Response Team complaints jumped 433% last week (4 complaints vs. 0.8 weekly average, z-score: 4.91), an unusual metric suggesting elevated emergency calls, welfare checks, or police/EMS incidents requiring investigation.
evidence: Emergency Response Team complaints: 4 last week vs. 0.8 weekly average (433% spike, z-score: 4.91)
Unclear whether this reflects increased incidents or resident complaints about ERT conduct; requires deeper sourcing
No corresponding spike in police or fire data provided, limiting ability to triangulate
reporting_angles: What incidents triggered the ERT complaints; were they welfare checks, mental health crises, or other emergency calls?
Are residents complaining about ERT response time, conduct, or frequency of activity in their neighborhoods?
